solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deem rent is not right, but settles

indicators.note: something not right is out of order, so these letters are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the rent is wrong but pays up anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' looks like a comment on the rent; it signals that DEEM, RENT and IS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a question is to decide it firmly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: They may be jellied or else cooked

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food that is either set in aspic or otherwise prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels are a traditional London East End dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End delicacy of jellied eels makes these fish an example of something jellied.

clue.text: Bearing blossom in March or April

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
an aster is a flower

explanation.surface: A tree in flower in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: This movable Christian festival always falls in March or April, so the definition describes its timing.

clue.text: Chaps most upset about ticks

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the chaps
upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men are very upset about blood-sucking parasites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the letters of 'most' and 'about' wraps them round the chaps; 'ticks' poses as parasites but means moments of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a brief instant, as in 'just a tick', so ticks are short spans of time.

clue.text: Money the school raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school collects funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is paper money, a specific form of it.

clue.text: He plans to no good purpose

definitions.text: He plans to no good purpose

parts.words: He plans to no good purpose
parts.note: reads as someone whose plans fail, but means a person who plots mischief

explanation.surface: A man whose plans come to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter who devises crafty or underhand plots fits a person planning for bad ends.

clue.text: The demon drink?

parts.note: the stock phrase for alcohol, read as a demon that is a liquor such as whisky

explanation.surface: A temperance warning about alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Strong liquor is called spirits, so a wicked one is both a demon and a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A malign supernatural being is a demon, and spirits are also strong drinks.

clue.text: Early form of rock music? Yes!

definitions.text: Early form of rock music? Yes!

parts.words: Early form of rock music? Yes!
parts.note: rock suggests rock and roll, but here it means rocking a baby to sleep

explanation.surface: Asking about the origins of rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby sung while rocking an infant is the earliest music a person hears.

clue.text: Girl right at all times

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who is always right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done always or at every moment is done forever, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Draw stumps in an evenly contested game

definitions.meaning: in cricket, drawing stumps ends play, so read literally the words say to bring a fixture to its end
a contest where the sides are nearly level

explanation.surface: Play is ended in a tight cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'draw stumps' means to pull up the wooden stumps and end play for the day; read as a verb plus noun, the answer means exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight, finely balanced contest is a common sporting idiom for this phrase.

clue.text: With a new clue I'd get the mathematician

indicators.note: a new version of the words means their letters are made into something fresh

parts.note: the contraction gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Rewriting a crossword clue reveals a famous mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek geometer of Alexandria is history's best-known writer on geometry, an example of a mathematician.

clue.text: They may be of untold value

definitions.text: They may be of untold value

parts.words: They may be of untold value
parts.note: untold suggests immeasurable worth, but literally means things not told to anyone

explanation.surface: Treasures whose worth is beyond reckoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept confidential are literally untold, which the clue dresses up as priceless.

clue.text: Dispatches produce merriment on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship means being inside it

parts.note: a ship is boarded, here the steamship abbreviation SS
laughter is merriment

explanation.surface: Messages produce amusement among those on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatches' looks like a noun for messages; it is the verb meaning kills.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch is to kill, so slaughtering is a synonym for dispatching.

clue.text: Document required when handing over a vehicle

definitions.meaning: a legal deed transferring property to a new owner
any means of transport such as a carriage

explanation.surface: Paperwork needed when selling a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal property-transfer deed and a means of transport share this word.

clue.text: Club that has lofty aims

parts.note: lofty aims suggests an ambitious society, but means a golf club with a high-lofted face

explanation.surface: An ambitious society or organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an old name for a golf wood, roughly a modern 3-wood, which lofts the ball high.
explanation.definitionFit: An old golf club with a lofted face sends the ball high, so it aims lofty.

clue.text: Again become invalid or again become an invalid

definitions.meaning: to lapse a second time, becoming void once more
to fall ill again after recovering

explanation.surface: A clue playing on two pronunciations of the same spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: INvalid (sick person) and inVALid (void) are spelt alike, so the two halves look identical but mean different things.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling back into illness or into a lapsed state are both senses of this word.

clue.text: It flies a welcome in the British Fleet

indicators.note: in places the greeting inside the navy abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
ave is a Latin greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A flag of welcome flown by the British navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black bird is an example of something that flies.

clue.text: Weapon made from spare parts

indicators.note: spare parts here are the letters of spare taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A weapon built from leftover components.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-shafted thrusting arm is a type of weapon.

clue.text: Coin a name for a royal governess

definitions.meaning: a former Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee

definitions.text: a name for a royal governess
definitions.meaning: the English governess at the Siamese court in The King and I bore this first name

explanation.surface: Inventing a name for a royal nanny.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an old Indian coin and the governess Leonowens of The King and I share this word.

clue.text: Old ship with a right to proceed

parts.note: to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: An old vessel given clearance to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason sailed this vessel in Greek myth, an example of an ancient ship.

clue.text: Codeword associated with Juliet

definitions.meaning: the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter R

explanation.surface: A secret word linked to a girl named Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet is itself a NATO alphabet codeword (J), which makes the link doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio alphabet's word for R and Shakespeare's young lover share this name.

clue.text: I write in red — not green

indicators.note: in places the first-person word and the writing verb inside red

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A teacher marks work in red ink, not green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' and 'green' look like rival ink colours; green here means unripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is no longer green, meaning unripe, has matured fully.

clue.text: Porridge going round at breakfast, say?

parts.note: a circle or ring is the shape O
breakfast is an example of a meal, signalled by say

explanation.surface: Porridge being served at breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge made from ground oats is a thick cereal dish of this name.

clue.text: Used in making her kind of pickle?

indicators.note: used in means the letters are contained within the following words

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone's favourite preserve went into a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pickled cucumber is a classic example of a pickle.

clue.text: Type of magenta identification label

indicators.note: a type of magenta suggests a variant form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badge printed in a purplish-red colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A small badge bearing someone's name is an identification label.

clue.text: Little creature of high birth

parts.note: high birth suggests nobility, but means a young bird hatched in a lofty eyrie

explanation.surface: A small aristocratic being.
explanation.definitionFit: A young raptor is born in a nest high on a cliff, literally a high birth.

clue.text: Sign name in a dazed state

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation goes inside the word for sign

parts.note: a trace is a sign or mark left behind

explanation.surface: Someone signs their name while dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotic, half-conscious condition is a dazed state.

clue.text: One member's naughty children

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP is a Member of Parliament; the possessive supplies the S

explanation.surface: A politician's badly behaved offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischievous little devils is a playful term for naughty children.

clue.text: Short of ammunition

parts.note: suggests running low on bullets, but means the abbreviated form of the word

explanation.surface: Troops running low on rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the informal clipped form of the word for bullets and shells.

clue.text: French writer's pseudonym

parts.note: the phrase is French for a writer's assumed name, literally pen name

explanation.surface: The assumed name of an author from France.
explanation.walkthrough: The French term is borrowed into English for any author's alias, so it need not be a French writer at all.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase, meaning pen name, is the standard term for an author's alias.

clue.text: Run for water

definitions.meaning: a mill channel carrying a swift current of water

explanation.surface: Dashing off to fetch something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a contest and a fast channel of water in a mill share this word.

clue.text: Not ideal, so may result in ruin

indicators.note: the letters given produce a new word as their result, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A warning that a poor situation could lead to disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of devastation and waste is a synonym for ruin.
